title: Tailoring microstructure and mechanical properties of 11Cr ferritic/martensitic steel via tempering
abstract: The multi-scale microstructure in 11Cr ferritic/martensitic (11Cr F/M) steel, including prior austenite grain, martensite substructure, carbides were tailoring by employing different tempering temperature from 700 to 800 °C. The microstructure, strength (room temperature and 550 °C) and hardness were investigated in detail as function of tempering temperature. The results reveal that tempering at 700 °C induced high-density dislocation, fine martensitic lath and carbides size which are responsible for higher yield strength ∼723 MPa and ∼ 565 MPa, and total elongation ∼18.8 % and ∼ 39.2 % at ambient temperature and 550 °C, respectively. Within the tempering temperature range, all samples underwent different degree of recovery and recrystallization. Compared to tempering at 700 °C, the martensitic lath width, M23C6 carbides size and volume fraction of MC carbides increased significantly, and the dislocation density decreased as tempering temperature increased. The enrichment of alloying elements in matrix was reduced, accompanied by the coarsening of M23C6 carbides at cost of sacrificing solid solution strengthening during tempering. The yield strength decreased with increasing tempering temperature, primarily due to the coarsening of martensitic lath, M23C6 carbides, which reduced contribution of subgrain boundary strengthening and precipitation strengthening. The strengthening effect was calculated in light of various strengthening mechanisms in 11Cr F/M steel. This study can hopefully enrich the understanding of microstructure evolution and mechanical properties in ferritic/martensitic steel during tempering.
